payload.answer: Proceed independently on TIMING, but not on MEANING. Blocking this project until job-lifecycle-commands lands would stall a fix that is currently blocking real work, so build now. But do not define a private CANCELLED: the state has exactly one meaning -- this job will not run again -- and what differs is only how it got there. Record that as provenance on the transition event (abandoned_with_project versus a direct operator stop), never as a second flavour of the state. The test that keeps the two honest is that a CANCELLED job is not claimable regardless of which path produced it. If job-lifecycle-commands later adds a state machine in domain/, this code should move onto it rather than keep a parallel implementation -- say so in the PR so the follow-up is visible instead of forgotten.
